passage:
When Ian got his first library card, he thought it was just a piece of plastic. His mother said it was more powerful than it looked.
"With this," she said, "you can take home stories, facts, pictures, and ideas."
Ian used the card to borrow a book about space. Then he borrowed one about insects, then one about cooking. Each book led him to another question.
One day, he forgot to return a book on time and had to pay a small fine. He became more careful after that.
The library card taught Ian two things. It gave him freedom to learn, but it also gave him responsibility. Borrowing something means bringing it back for the next person.
